articleTitle: Safety and reliability of medium voltage switchgear with solid insulation of present day and future design
publicationTitle: 1990 Third International Conference on Future Trends in Distribution Switchgear
abstract: The authors give a review of the design philosophy of insulation-enclosed switchgear. Attention is paid to specific requirements for the insulation enclosure as laid down in IEC standards, in order to guarantee safety and reliability during its life time. Experience with this system, acquired over many years of service, is described. The authors then give a short description of the use of epoxy resin for a future RMU design, equipped with an integrated earthing system, full range fuses, vacuum load-break switches or alternatively vacuum circuit-breakers. The maintenance requirements and the area of application are specified. They also make some remarks concerning the Dutch cable network and its reliability, as well as some general comments on switchgear and the environment.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The 'failure to break' test in MV switchboards: an improvement of safety of persons and property
publicationTitle: 1990 Third International Conference on Future Trends in Distribution Switchgear
abstract: The authors indicate the Electricite de France policy concerning the ability of 24 kV switchboards for public distribution to withstand an internal arc. The technical specification requires particularly a 'failure to break' test in addition to the IEC requirements. The power test facilities of Les Renardieres High Power Laboratory (LEP) have made it possible to define and demonstrate the validity of effective technological solutions before using the equipment on the network.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Micro-controller for substation and network automation
publicationTitle: 1990 Third International Conference on Future Trends in Distribution Switchgear
abstract: The South East Queensland Electricity Board (SEQEB) has been evaluating various approaches to reducing the cost of distributing electricity. The Micro Controller is a device designed to be installed on feeders and transformers at bulk and zone substations. It is a stand alone mini SCADA system which also carries out protection functions including: overcurrent, earthfault, sensitive earthfault, auto reclose, and circuit breaker fail protection. It also provides current and voltage indication, alarm annunciation and data logging. The authors review the design and application of the Micro Controller in detail, with information on installation, commissioning and operational experience gained to data.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Influence of TRV network on circuit breaker interruption performance at terminal fault conditions
publicationTitle: 1990 Third International Conference on Future Trends in Distribution Switchgear
abstract: The effects of reignitions after interruption of short-circuit currents at very short arcing times has been found as a possible source of overvoltages. These overvoltages will occur when the circuit breaker being tested is able to interrupt the periodic high-frequency discharge currents, which come from the TRV network. Field tests have show that cable and line networks will produce periodic high-frequency discharge currents. The network for the TRV representation must be able to produce a periodic high-frequency discharge current. Future IEC specifications should take these effects into account for a correct definition of test conditions.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Failure analysis of circuit breakers in the Upper Egypt Zone of the Egyptian Unified Power System network
publicationTitle: 1990 Third International Conference on Future Trends in Distribution Switchgear
abstract: The authors present the results and the major findings of a research study conducted to investigate circuit breaker failures in the Upper Egypt Zone of the Egyptian Unified Power System network for the 66 kV, 33 kV, 11 kV, and 6.6 kV voltage levels. The total population of circuit breakers considered in this study is 881 distributed per location as: 107 indoor and 774 outdoor, per voltage level as: 89, 220, 524 and 48 for the 66 kV, 33 kV, 11 kV and 6.6 kV respectively and per interrupter as: 747 oil, 85 air and 49 of other types.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Trends in distribution transformer protection
publicationTitle: 1990 Third International Conference on Future Trends in Distribution Switchgear
abstract: Until the 1960s, ground-mounted, cable connected distribution transformers were usually supplied from oil circuit-breakers with trip coils operated directly from current transformers in the connections to the transformer. Time grading was provided by short-circuiting the trip coils by special fuses, usually referred to as time limit fuses. The development of the HV fuse in the late 1950s led to the creation of the fuse-switch and this brought about a cheaper solution to the protection of distribution transformers. In more recent times the technology of switching devices is undergoing change with the introduction of SF/sub 6/ as the insulating and arc control medium in place of oil. These new designs of equipment introduce the possibility of re-examining the techniques and economics of transformer protection which the authors attempt to do.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Distribution substation switchgear-a necessary evil?
publicationTitle: 1990 Third International Conference on Future Trends in Distribution Switchgear
abstract: The author briefly discusses the historical background and practices in distribution substation switchgear. The reasons for including 11 kV switchgear at a distribution transformer point and discussed. Possible future developments in substation switchgear are discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An advancement in the design and application of current-limiting fuses
publicationTitle: 1990 Third International Conference on Future Trends in Distribution Switchgear
abstract: The authors outline a new concept in the design of a current-limiting fuse using modern technology. Design, development and testing aspects are described in some detail. Present and future applications of this product are also discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: 72 kV C-GIS composite insulation in SF/sub 6/ gas
publicationTitle: 1990 Third International Conference on Future Trends in Distribution Switchgear
abstract: For further reduction in installation space, the authors have developed a second generation C-GIS (cubicle gas insulated switchgear) which makes use of a composite insulation of low pressure SF/sub 6/ gas and solid material. The new C-GIS has realized a reduction in installation space of about 50% from conventional C-GIS. The authors introduce a gas-solid composite insulation employed in the C-GIS, and a new technique that eliminates the need to recharge the insulation gas into the cubicle during the site erection, contributing to shortening the installation period while maintaining its reliability. An overview of the second generation C-GIS is given.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Low voltage assemblies of switchgear and control-gear comparison of UK and continental European practice
publicationTitle: 1990 Third International Conference on Future Trends in Distribution Switchgear
abstract: BS5486 Part 1 1986 'Low Voltage Switchgear and Controlgear Assemblies' is identical to IEC 439-1 1985 which will shortly be accepted as a Euro-Norm (EN). This means that the constructional rules contained therein are acceptable in the single European Market. IEC439-1 is also acceptable in many overseas countries, for example, Australia and the Far East. Based upon these standards the author compares UK and European practice concerning short circuit protection requirements, discrimination and co-ordination, electric shock protection and insulated assemblies.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Remote controlled overhead switchgear in association with fault indicator-M2S
publicationTitle: 1990 Third International Conference on Future Trends in Distribution Switchgear
abstract: In order to improve the quality of electrical supply in rural areas, it is necessary to find equipment to isolate the faulty part of the feeder very rapidly. A new type of overhead switchgear is developed in association with fault indicator to improve reliability and availability and to make erection easier. Mounting on only one base of the switch-disconnector, the operating device, surge arresters and MV/LV transformer for control gear, and auxiliary equipment is assembled in the factory. The system can be remotely controlled, in the case of extreme climatic conditions.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Switch (sectionalizer) for distribution automation system
publicationTitle: 1990 Third International Conference on Future Trends in Distribution Switchgear
abstract: The distribution automation system (DAS) is a system to provide remote control and supervising switches on a high-voltage distribution line for switching load current of the line either automatically or manually. The DAS is widely used in Japan and requires an automatic switch (sectionalizer) which Toshiba has continuously supplied since 1977. The authors introduce the automatic switch based on their experiences.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Preparation for 1992 and beyond-the distribution Technology Park-a practical application of new equipment and systems
publicationTitle: 1990 Third International Conference on Future Trends in Distribution Switchgear
abstract: The Distribution Technology Park opened at Colchester in April 1989. The authors gives the background to its origin and records progress.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Requirement-oriented medium-voltage switchgear in urban networks
publicationTitle: 1990 Third International Conference on Future Trends in Distribution Switchgear
abstract: Interruptions in the electricity supply to the customers are mainly caused by faults in the medium-voltage network. Some 80% of non-delivered energy and nondelivered power can be attributed to such faults. So when reductions in the cost and space requirements of medium-voltage switchgear are being considered, the effects of such reductions on the reliability of supply to the customers must be taken into account. Network and installation configurations must always be considered in context. Within the framework of such integrated networks and installation planning, simplified medium-voltage switchgear was devised and has been successfully implemented within the TWS network. These installations are the subject of the paper.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A reliable, low maintenance dead break disconnection unit for the modern distribution system
publicationTitle: 1990 Third International Conference on Future Trends in Distribution Switchgear
abstract: The electrical supply industry's requirements for a simple low maintenance dead break T disconnector for the MV cable distribution system was met by the MK I Raychem Disconnect Unit. Experience with this unit suggested several detail improvements to the basic design which would make it smaller, easier to install and faster to operate. The authors describe the MK II design and several of its applications.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Ring main switchgear-expectation and solution
publicationTitle: 1990 Third International Conference on Future Trends in Distribution Switchgear
abstract: The author describes a new generation of distribution equipment which does indeed seek to retain present value and add further improvement. These advantages accrue in the areas of safety and maintenance. An SF/sub 6/ filled ring main unit aimed at the elimination of degradation and flammability of the filling medium is described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Future developments in SF/sub 6/ circuit-breakers and their likely benefits on users
publicationTitle: 1990 Third International Conference on Future Trends in Distribution Switchgear
abstract: The use of SF/sub 6/ puffer circuit-breakers is now well established throughout the complete range of high voltage and medium voltage applications. These circuit-breakers have established an excellent service record in reliability and efficiency. Manufacturers have investigated the possibility of other SF/sub 6/ interruption techniques which might offer further benefits. In particular, considerable efforts have been made to reduce the required operating energy, further reduce contact erosion and to allow operation at very low SF/sub 6/ filling pressures. The techniques considered are that of rotating arc and autoexpansion. The rotating arc is described only briefly. Autoexpansion (the combination of rotating arc and self expansion) however is relatively new and is therefore discussed in some detail.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: 40 kA 15 kV class vacuum switchgear for power station auxiliaries and distribution systems
publicationTitle: 1990 Third International Conference on Future Trends in Distribution Switchgear
abstract: A range of 40 kA switchgear has been developed to meet the requirements of power station auxiliaries an heavy industry, including the oil production platforms in the North Sea. The equipment meets the requirements of the most stringent safety rules and working practices which apply to this class of equipment, particularly for access to equipment where adjacent parts contain live conductors.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Distribution fuses of nearest future
publicationTitle: 1990 Third International Conference on Future Trends in Distribution Switchgear
abstract: Low investment costs and reliable operation, particularly as a short-circuit protection make distribution fuses indispensable in distribution systems. To keep pace with modern system requirements, distribution fuses need to be improved to be competitive with other overcurrent protections. Improvements are required to overcome the following problems. HRC fuses: drastic reduction of the rated power losses, cut-off currents, operating I/sup 2/t and overvoltages; and creation of new more economical versions of full-range fuses. Gas-expulsion fuses: design of the gas-expulsion distribution fuses able to interrupt unlimitedly small overcurrents; and creation of sparkless gas-expulsion distribution fuses. The state of fuse technology and investigations make possible implementation of these improvements without paying too great a price. The author discusses the problems mentioned and gives some results of the investigations which could be useful by detailed solving of those problems.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Increasing the fire safety of distribution switchgear with fire-resistant hydrocarbon fluids
publicationTitle: 1990 Third International Conference on Future Trends in Distribution Switchgear
abstract: Fire-resistant hydrocarbon fluids have been shown to be an excellent arc-extinguishing media that are very resistant to fire and explosion. These characteristics, combined with their lubricity and biodegradability properties, make them a natural choice when evaluating dielectric fluids for use where the risk of fire must be minimized. New methods of refining and manufacturing these fluids are improving their heat transfer and electrical characteristics while maintaining their environmental acceptance. These improved fluids will assure the design engineer and electrical equipment owner of the ability to choose and maintain state of the art dielectric fluids well into the next century.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Philosophy of overpressure relief in gas filled distribution switchgear
publicationTitle: 1990 Third International Conference on Future Trends in Distribution Switchgear
abstract: In view of the ever increasing requirements for safety of the public and operators the author proposes that a means to allow the controlled relief of overpressure become mandatory for SF/sub 6/ metal-enclosed distribution switchgear enclosures. The author also proposes that the manufacturer demonstrates that in the unlikely event of an internal arcing fault of rated short-circuit current the gas enclosure shall rupture in a defined manner to allow the controlled relief and discharge of the arcing products.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The potential of optical fibre based methods for in-service switchgear monitoring
publicationTitle: 1990 Third International Conference on Future Trends in Distribution Switchgear
abstract: The monitoring of in-service circuit breakers is limited and there is a persuasive argument that such monitoring is unnecessary and not cost effective. The need for better monitoring is often only recognised following accidents such as environment threatening oil spillage or explosion hazards from gas leakages. If a more extensive monitoring philosophy is to be implemented consideration needs to be given to the most effective technology for this purpose. One important candidate is that based upon optical fibre sensing. Such systems offer many advantages for circuit breaker monitoring and are already well developed for monitoring in other supply industries. The authors discuss the potential of these methods for switchgear monitoring.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Trends and concepts of MV switchgear and a look into the future
publicationTitle: 1990 Third International Conference on Future Trends in Distribution Switchgear
abstract: The author discusses the existing demands on primary and secondary distribution stations and the presently available practical solutions. Future trends are examined and their possible impact on the design of switchgear, including control, monitoring and protection equipment is discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new microprocessor relay for overhead line SCADA applications
publicationTitle: 1990 Third International Conference on Future Trends in Distribution Switchgear
abstract: Overhead line power systems are by their very nature extremely susceptible to transient faults. To reduce system interruption to a minimum, intelligent devices such as auto reclosers are used to clear these faults and maintain supply to healthy sections of network. The relay described is designed for use with the PMR range of auto reclosers produced by Brush Switchgear Limited. The aim is to produce a new generation of auto reclose relays which is ideally suited for application to overhead line system control and automation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Computer simulation of prestriking transients in cable-connected motor systems
publicationTitle: 1990 Third International Conference on Future Trends in Distribution Switchgear
abstract: A computer program used for calculating multiple prestriking transients in three-phase cable connected motor systems, and which is based on Fourier solution methods is described. It is demonstrated that the complex interaction taking place between individual poles of the closing switch can be successfully simulated. It is also shown that, in a given system, a wide range of prestriking transients can be produced by variation in mechanical pole closure scatter of the poles of the switching device. In particular, it is demonstrated that under certain pole closure sequences, the greatest prestriking transients can be produced by the last pole of the switching device to close.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Swedish distribution networks-aspects on neutral treatment, earthfault clearance and related matters
publicationTitle: 1990 Third International Conference on Future Trends in Distribution Switchgear
abstract: The Swedish State Power Board has been studying different earthfault protection schemes in order to improve the existing concepts. A number of its current research projects are also related to the question of neutral treatment in distribution networks. The authors discusses some general views on the matter and gives a short presentation of one of the current projects. The project in question deals with the aspect of high impedance fault detection in plants with covered overhead lines.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Effect of 1992 single market. Practice, plan and people
publicationTitle: 1990 Third International Conference on Future Trends in Distribution Switchgear
abstract: The author looks at the effect of the 1992 single market in Europe on MV circuit breakers. The different voltages used in the European community are discussed and the commercial strategy of various companies is presented. The selling of circuit breakers is also looked at.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
